newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH SAY PLATT DEAL AGREED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH SAY PLATT DEAL AGREED.

text.p: Middlesbrough said on Thursday Arsenal had accepted their bid for former England skipper David Platt.
However, Arsenal said nothing had been formally settled, although they had given Middlesbrough permission to talk to the 31-year-old midfielder.
"Bryan Robson told me he had had a bid accepted by Arsenal," a Middlesbrough spokesman said.
Club sources said the deal was expected to be in the two million pounds ($3.2 million) bracket, with Platt and Robson due to discuss personal terms later on Thursday.
Platt, who joined Arsenal from Italy's Sampdoria two years ago, would be following team mate Paul Merson to newly-relegated Middlesbrough.
Middlesbrough, consigned to the first division at the end of last season, recently signed Merson from the north London club in a five million pounds ($8 million) deal.
Arsenal confirmed on Thursday they had reached an agreement with Monaco to sign Liberian striker Christopher Wreh, a cousin of AC Milan and Liberia marksman George Weah.
